records.applicability: http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 is in the Admin application graph only through development tooling: @angular/cli 21.2.28 -> pacote 21.5.1 -> make-fetch-happen 15.0.6 (via npm-registry-fetch 19.1.1, sigstore/@sigstore/sign 4.1.1 and tuf-js 4.1.0, all integrity-identical to the 2026-10-07 measurement). It is not in the production bundle. make-fetch-happen/lib/cache/policy.js is its only requirer and builds every CachePolicy with { shared: false, ignoreCargoCult: true }; the advisory's mechanism needs a shared cache. Measured 2026-10-23 on e864c826 (Node 20, offline, preload probe with positive controls): ng version, eslint ., ng build --configuration=production and ng test (842/842) loaded neither http-cache-semantics, make-fetch-happen nor pacote. Package operations (ng add, ng update) were source-traced, not exercised. This does not cover a consumer that constructs a shared cache.
records.reason: As of 2026-10-23 no fixed release exists: the advisory lists no patched version and 4.3.0 is the latest release. 4.3.0 is outside the recorded range but leaves the max-stale and shared Set-Cookie handling byte-identical, so it is not a fix and is not installed. Removing the package means an Angular major (22, Node >=22.22.3), which is not a dependency fix. Without a disposition the measured application graph is blocking. The accepted residual risk is that a traced-but-unexercised tooling consumer behaves differently from the measured runs. Remove this record in the same change that installs a release fixing the mechanism or removes the package; it expires at 00:00 UTC on 2026-12-31 and is not extended automatically.

records.applicability: undici 7.29.1 is in the Admin application graph only because @angular/build 21.2.28 (a devDependency) pins it exactly ("undici": "7.29.1"; 21.2.25 to 21.2.28 all do, and 21.2.28 is the latest 21.2.x). It is not in the production bundle. Its only requirer in the graph is @angular/build/src/tools/vite/plugins/ssr-ssl-plugin.js, which the dev server adds only when SSR is enabled (createAngularServerSideSSLPlugin, ssrMode !== NoSsr) and which then installs a global Agent carrying extra CA certificates; angular.json configures no ssr, server, prerender or outputMode. The advisory's mechanism needs undici to decode an HTTP response carrying excessive content-encodings. Measured 2026-10-24 on the #48 lock (Node 20.20.0, a load probe on CommonJS and ESM resolution with positive controls for require, import, a worker thread and a child process): ng version, eslint ., ng build --configuration=production and ng test (842/842) resolved no file under node_modules/undici. ng serve was source-traced, not exercised. This does not cover an SSR-enabled dev server.
records.reason: As of 2026-10-24 a fixed release exists (7.30.1, published 2026-10-15) but cannot be installed without changing package.json: @angular/build pins 7.29.1 exactly, including the latest 21.2.28, and this repository uses no overrides. The node-gyp copy (6.29.0 to 6.29.1) is fixed in the lock in the same change. Without a disposition the measured application graph is blocking. The accepted residual risk is that a traced-but-unexercised dev-server path loads undici. Remove this record in the same change that installs an @angular/build that no longer pins a vulnerable undici; it expires at 00:00 UTC on 2026-11-30 and is not extended automatically.

records.applicability: undici 6.29.0 is bundled inside the pinned scanner, npm 11.21.1, which is installed from dependency-audit/scanner with scripts disabled and run only as npm audit. Its only requirer in the bundle is node_modules/node-gyp/lib/download.js (node-gyp 12.4.0, header downloads for native builds), which npm audit does not invoke; npm's registry requests go through npm-registry-fetch and make-fetch-happen. Measured 2026-10-24 (Node 20.20.0, the same load probe and controls): the scanner's exact audit argv, against the application graph and against its own graph, resolved no file under node_modules/undici and returned complete reports. A scanner that crashed would leave the audit incomplete, which fails closed.
records.reason: As of 2026-10-24 no npm release for Node 20 bundles a fixed undici: 11.21.1 is the latest 11.x and bundles 6.29.0 (fixed in 6.29.1, published 2026-10-15), and npm 12.x requires Node 22. Without a disposition the scanner graph is blocking. The accepted residual risk is that the scanner loads undici on a path the measured runs did not take. Remove this record in the same change that moves the scanner to an npm that bundles undici 6.29.1 or later; it expires at 00:00 UTC on 2026-11-30 and is not extended automatically.
